headline: High: AutoGPT can write locally while dexter has broad network/API access, creating dangerous default pathways for leakage, conflicts, and unverified downstream actions.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGPT exposes filesystem and agent-protocol I/O, while dexter writes to .dexter/scratchpad/ and uses autonomous execution. That creates a plausible default bridge where one agent can consume the other's file outputs as instructions. No shared channel is explicitly documented, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF AutoGPT reads dexter scratchpad files as prompts or instructions
IF dexter ingests AutoGPT-generated files without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate the two agents into different directories
Disable automatic file ingestion between agents
Add a manual review step before either agent reads the other's outputs
Use read-only mounts for shared artifacts
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging on exchanged files

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGPT has filesystem access and allowlisted egress; dexter has broad network egress, multiple external APIs, and handles financial and market data plus several secrets. Even without a shared workspace explicitly proven, the pair can move sensitive local artifacts into outbound API calls, so the leakage pathway exists in default-style operation.
conditions: IF AutoGPT places sensitive files into dexter's scratchpad
IF dexter forwards scratchpad contents or context to OpenAI, Exa, Tavily, or Financial Datasets APIs
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of shared working directories
Restrict dexter API calls to non-sensitive queries
Rotate and scope API keys before pairing
Disable file-based context ingestion for dexter
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention filters on outbound prompts

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGPT can execute shell commands and spawn subprocesses, and dexter supports multiple instances with autonomous execution and broad network egress. Both can mutate local state or external resources, so overlapping writes and race conditions are plausible. The lack of explicit locking or coordination means the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same filesystem path
IF both agents modify the same external API-backed resource without locks
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Serialize writes with a simple operator-managed lock file
Run only one agent at a time for mutable tasks
Make shared resources read-only
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination for shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGPT can generate outputs from shell-driven workflows, and dexter's autonomous execution plus external APIs make it likely to act on upstream results. Because dexter is not documented here as verifying AutoGPT's outputs, the pair can cascade errors from one agent into the other's actions. Uncertainty about verification raises this to medium.
conditions: IF dexter treats AutoGPT-produced text as authoritative
IF AutoGPT emits incorrect facts that dexter uses in API calls or reports
mitigations: Require human review before dexter acts on AutoGPT output
Add a verification checklist for factual claims
Limit dexter to drafting rather than executing actions
Log source provenance alongside each handoff
requires-engineering: implement confidence or citation validation gates

E_compliance.rationale: dexter explicitly touches financial and market data and requests many API keys, while AutoGPT has filesystem access and allowlisted egress. The profiles do not show a residency or certification mismatch directly, but the combination creates a plausible compliance gap if regulated data is routed through AutoGPT's local files or dexter's third-party APIs. Uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF regulated financial data is written into AutoGPT-accessible files
IF dexter sends regulated data to third-party APIs without a DPA or retention controls
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared files
Review API vendor terms before use
Disable logging of sensitive prompts and outputs
Use synthetic or redacted datasets for pairing
requires-engineering: add residency and retention policy enforcement
